items.t: Mt. Lehman real estate guide
Condo stock concentrates in four pockets: Gladwin Road beside Mill Lake, Simon Avenue in Clearbrook, South Fraser Way downtown, and Montrose Avenue in Historic Downtown.
Gladwin Road sits under the City Centre Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2913-2019); Montrose Avenue under the Historic Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Bylaw 2920-2019).
Mahogany at Mill Lake, 2180 Gladwin Road, is the core's concrete tower: 27 storeys, 152 suites, by Quantum Properties.
Regency Park, 3170 Gladwin Road (listings also use 3150 Gladwin Road), is a 1990 high-rise of 188 units; Lakewood Gardens, 2491 Gladwin Road, a 1989 low-rise of 39 units.
Historic Downtown's Urban 1 – Midrise designation permits up to six storeys: the form of Montvue, 33820 South Fraser Way, and The Mason, 2771 Montrose Avenue.
Simon Avenue holds Auburn, 32528 Simon Avenue, and Trethewey Tower, 32440 Simon Avenue; Town Centre Tower, 32330 South Fraser Way, dates to 1993.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Rental-restriction bylaws are unenforceable: since November 24, 2022 no strata may restrict long-term rentals, even where a directory still records "rentals not allowed" (Regency Park, Lakewood Gardens).
The only enforceable age bylaw is 55-plus (55+), under Strata Property Act sections 123.1 and 123.2; any lower stated age is invalid.
Zoning Bylaw No. 2400-2014 governs; the 2025 updates raised the Mid Rise Apartment Zone (RMM) to 2.5 Floor Space Ratio and stopped counting hallways, elevators and stairwells as floor area.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Aria, 33538 Cottage Lane, looks like the core's newest condo building but is a rental apartment building, not strata condos.
The City is realigning Montvue Avenue and building West Railway Plaza at Essendene Avenue — the blocks around The Mason and Montvue are a construction zone by design.
Montvue's counts conflict: the project architect counts 90 units in two five-storey buildings; presale directories describe 110 condominiums in two six-storey buildings.
Clearbrook Waterworks District homes are billed quarterly for sewer only, unlike the bi-monthly combined billing elsewhere in the city.
The Mason is the first condo building in The Rail District, the former Clayburn Brick Plant lands between Pine Street and Morey Avenue — later phases are still to come.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos: development and new projects

items.t: Rezone to Mid Rise Apartment Zone (RMM), Bylaw No. 3678-2025; $290,488 Community Amenity Contribution. Status: before Council for first, second and third readings, September 16, 2025 (as of November 3, 2026).

Highstreet Village condominiums — Cardinal Avenue at Mt. Lehman Road; developer: Highstreet Village (Shape Properties); home type: condominiums within a 131-townhome, 9-condominium-building community; current release: The Sunset Collection. Status: building out in phases (as of November 3, 2026).
2026 property tax rates are set by Tax Rates Bylaw No. 3727-2026, per $1,000 of taxable value; a strata unit is taxed on its own assessed value.
Water and sewer are metered: from March 1, 2026, water is $1.46 per cubic metre and sewer $1.35; whether strata fees include them is stated on the Form B.
Abbotsford is a listed taxable area for the provincial Speculation and Vacancy Tax; every residential owner must declare annually.
New condos carry 5 percent Goods and Services Tax (GST); resales do not. The Newly Built Home Exemption removes Property Transfer Tax in full up to $1,100,000, partially to $1,150,000.
Downtown condos anchor on Bourquin Exchange, where BC Transit routes 1, 2, 4, 5, 12, 17, 21 and 31 meet; route 5 (Clearbrook / Bourquin via Hospital) is the Gladwin Road hospital link.
Route 66, the Fraser Valley Express, connects Abbotsford with Langley and Burnaby (Lougheed Station) via Highway 1 and expanded service on January 4, 2026.
Highstreet Exchange construction began January 4, 2026; routes 1, 2 and 66 were detoured to a temporary exchange on Cardinal Avenue.

blocks.text: Abbotsford Condos: risks and due diligence

items.t: Start with the depreciation report on any pre-2000 building: the first mandatory cycle lands on the Gladwin Road and Simon Avenue stock's roof, piping and parkade years.
Check the Form B for approved special levies still payable and the CRF balance; the strata must provide it within seven days, maximum $35 plus copying.
Flood geography matters at the city's edges: Sumas Prairie flooded in December 2025 (485 properties under Evacuation Order), and the City states a Matsqui Prairie flood would be worse.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Abbotsford?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board figures showed 546 condos and townhomes listed in Abbotsford and 89 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 16%. Month-end counts move daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: What is the reported sale price for condos and townhomes in Abbotsford?
faq.a: The October report gave $440,000 for condos and townhomes in Abbotsford, against $497,500 the month before. The reports give one sale-price figure and do not say whether it is an average or a median, so use it for direction, not as a valuation of your own home.

faq.q: How long do condos and townhomes take to sell in Abbotsford?
faq.a: The October report showed 30 days on market for condos and townhomes in Abbotsford and a sale-to-list price ratio of 98%, against 32 days the month before.

faq.q: What should I read before buying a condo in Abbotsford?
faq.a: The Form B, the bylaws, the last two years of strata minutes, the depreciation report and the contingency reserve fund balance. They show planned repairs, special levies and rules on pets and rentals.

faq.q: What do strata fees cover on a condo in Abbotsford?
faq.a: Strata fees pay for upkeep and insurance of the common property and the contingency reserve fund, and in some buildings heat, hot water or other services. The Form B Information Certificate lists exactly what a unit's fee covers.
